description: Heel slides guide: a gentle lying move for the lower abdominals and hip flexors that keeps your back still, with mistakes and easier or harder versions.
intro: Heel slides are a gentle lying move: slide one heel away along the floor and back. They teach the deep lower abdominals to keep your pelvis and back steady while a leg moves. The load is low and easy to control, so they are often used early, for example after childbirth once cleared.
feel: You should feel light work low in your belly and at the front of the moving hip, while your lower back and pelvis stay quiet. Breathe out as the heel slides away and in as it returns. Avoid breath holding, belly bulging or pushing down into the pelvis. Self-check: a hand under your lower back should feel the pressure stay about the same.

mistakes.wrong: Arching your back as the leg straightens
mistakes.right: Slide only as far as your back stays still, stopping before it lifts.
Use a light draw-in of the lower belly, not a crunch. You should still be able to talk.

mistakes.wrong: Rocking the pelvis side to side
mistakes.right: Keep both hip bones level and move slowly enough to notice any tilt.

easier: Slide only halfway, or put a towel under your heel so it glides more easily.
harder: Slide out more slowly, hover the heel just off the floor, or add a gentle Kegel on the exhale.
who: People after childbirth once cleared, people over 50, and anyone rebuilding core control after a break.
skip: After a C-section, abdominal surgery or with separated abdominal muscles, ask your doctor or physiotherapist when to start. If you see doming along the middle of your belly, make the move smaller or pause it. Stop if it hurts.

faq.q: Are heel slides good after having a baby?
faq.a: They are a common early move because they are gentle and done lying down. Start once your doctor or physiotherapist clears you, and stop if you notice pain or doming.

faq.q: Why do my hip flexors feel it?
faq.a: The front of the hip moves the leg, so some effort there is normal. If it feels like strain, keep the slide slower and smaller.
